tool.name: disassembler msa
tool.description: reference-guided codon alignment and phylogeny of haplotypes

param.name: input
param.label: Haplotypes
param.help: Reconstructed or thinned haplotypes, in reference orientation.

param.label: Minimum length relative to the reference
param.help: Sequences shorter than this fraction of the reference length are left out of the alignment.

tool.help:
@HELP_SUITE@
-----
What it does ************
Builds an in-frame codon alignment of haplotypes against a reference CDS, then a maximum-likelihood phylogeny from it.
Each haplotype is added to the reference with MAFFT ``--keeplength --addfragments``, so the alignment keeps exactly the reference's length and coordinates. Insertions relative to the reference are dropped, the reading frame stays fixed, and every column is a reference position. The tool checks that every aligned sequence has the reference's length, then infers a tree with FastTree under the GTR model.
Sequence names are reduced to letters, digits and underscores (at most 40 characters) so they are safe in Newick. The reference appears as ``Reference``.
Note on LexicMap route inputs: **disassembler lexicmap** already emits a reference-coordinate MSA as part of its multi-HSP tiling. Every row is the reference length, with no gaps and no Ns, because the clean cohort gates (``--require-full-length``, ``--min-pident``, ``--max-internal-stops``) only let through accessions whose tiled sequence sits on the reference grid without needing an insertion. On three real cohorts (``erg11`` collapsed, ``erg11`` per-accession, SARS-CoV-2 spike collapsed; 27 to 14,594 sequences) re-running MAFFT ``--auto`` on the lexicmap output reproduced it byte-for-byte, every row and every column. So on the LexicMap route this tool is a no-op and can be skipped: feed ``clean.msa.fasta`` straight to a tree builder. It still has to run on the walker route, whose per-accession reconstructions are not pre-aligned.
-----
Inputs ******
- **Haplotypes**: for example the reconstructed haplotypes from **disassembler walker**, the clean accessions from **disassembler lexicmap**, or the output of **disassembler sieve**. - **Reference CDS**: the in-frame coding sequence used upstream. Only the first record is used.
-----
Outputs *******
- **Codon alignment**: the reference followed by every haplotype that passed the length filter, all of the reference's length. - **Tree**: FastTree GTR phylogeny in Newick format.
